1.01 Get answers faster A vague question gets a vague answer. Four short lines fix that. Learn pivot tables in 10 minutes Think of an AI chatbot as a smart new joiner on day one. It knows a lot. It knows nothing about you, your job or what you want. If you say "explain pivot tables", you get a textbook answer. Give it a short brief instead. Use four parts: Role (who it should act as), Task (what to do), Context (what it needs to know about you) and Format (how the answer should look). You do not need fancy words. Plain sentences work. The more specific each part is, the less you edit afterwards. Use any free chatbot for this course: ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok or Claude. The prompts work in all of them. The wording of the answers will differ a little. Role: You are a patient Google Sheets trainer.
Task: Teach me what a pivot table is and how to make my first one.
Context: I use Google Sheets daily for simple lists and totals. I have never used a pivot table. I have a sheet with columns Date, Salesperson, Region and Amount.
Format: Give me 1) a one-sentence definition, 2) exactly 5 numbered steps to build a pivot table that shows total Amount for each Region, 3) one common mistake to avoid. Keep it under 150 words.
Show one example of what you want

1.02 Get answers faster One short example teaches the AI your tone better than ten adjectives. Turn a rude message into a polite one Words like "professional but friendly" mean different things to different people. An example removes the guesswork. This is often called few-shot prompting . It simply means: show it a sample first. Paste one or two samples of writing you like. Then say: "Match this tone." The AI copies the length, the warmth and the style. Keep the sample short. Three or four lines is enough. Remove names and private details before you paste anything. Never paste passwords or bank details into a chatbot. Rewrite my message so it is polite and clear. Match the tone of the example.

Example of the tone I like:
"Hi Meera, thanks for sending the draft. Could you share the final version by Thursday 5 PM? That lets me check it before the review. Thank you!"

My message:
"You are always late with the files. Send them on time from now on."

Rules: Keep it under 45 words. Do not blame the person. Include a clear deadline: Wednesday 4 PM. Give me only the rewritten message.
Get the format you need: tables, lists, limits

1.03 Get answers faster Ask for a table and you can decide in one glance. Compare two laptops in one table AI writes long paragraphs by default. That is slow to read on a phone. You can ask for exactly the shape you need. Useful format words: table with columns , numbered steps , 3 bullet points , under 80 words , one-line verdict at the end . When you compare options, always ask for a table plus a verdict. A table forces the AI to use the same points for each option. A verdict tells you what it would pick and why. Compare these two laptops for a person who does spreadsheets, email and video calls for 8 hours a day.

Laptop A: 16 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD, 1.3 kg, battery 12 hours, price Rs 62,000.
Laptop B: 8 GB RAM, 512 GB SSD, 1.8 kg, battery 7 hours, price Rs 48,000.

Format: a table with columns Feature, Laptop A, Laptop B, Better for office work. Use 5 rows: RAM, Weight, Battery, Price, Overall. After the table, write a one-line verdict starting with "Verdict:". Use only the facts I gave. Do not add specs.
Fix a bad answer with follow-ups

1.04 Get answers faster The first answer is a draft. The second message is where the quality comes from. Improve your profile bio by letting the AI interview you Most people read the first answer, feel disappointed and give up. Do this instead: talk to the chatbot like you would to a colleague. Say what is wrong and ask for a change. Three follow-ups that work almost every time: "Make it shorter." "Ask me what you need to know before you answer." "Give me 3 different versions." The second one is the strongest. Let the AI interview you. It spots the gaps in your brief that you did not see. Here is my current professional bio:
"I am a hard working person with 4 years of experience in office work. I am good at many things and I am a team player."

Do not rewrite it yet. First, ask me exactly 3 short questions that will help you make it specific and believable. Number the questions. Wait for my answers.
Check the facts: stop made-up answers

1.05 Get answers faster AI sounds sure even when it is wrong. You can make it show its doubts. Explain GST in simple words, and flag what to verify AI writes the most likely next words. It does not look facts up the way a search engine does. Sometimes it states something false in a calm, confident voice. People call this a hallucination . You cannot remove the risk. You can lower it. Ask the AI to label what it is sure about, to say what you should verify, and to name where to verify it. Some tools can also search the web. When they do, ask for the links and open them. Rule for work: never send a number, a date, a rule or a name to other people without checking it at the original source. This takes two minutes and protects your name. Explain what GST (Goods and Services Tax) is in India, for a new employee in an accounts-adjacent role.

Rules:
1. Write 4 bullet points, each under 20 words.
2. After each bullet, add a tag: [Sure] if it is a basic well-known idea, or [Verify] if it may change (rates, limits, deadlines, forms).
3. At the end, list 2 official places where I should verify the [Verify] items.
4. If you are not sure about something, say "I am not sure" instead of guessing.
Write the follow-up email in two minutes

2.01 Automate office work Give the facts. Let the AI do the wording. You do the final check. Chase a payment confirmation politely Emails are the easiest place to save time. The pattern is simple: you supply the facts (who, what, when), the goal (what you want them to do) and the tone . The AI writes the sentences. Always ask for two or three versions: short, normal and firm. Pick one and edit it. This is faster than editing one long draft. Before you send: read it once out loud, check the names, dates and amounts, and remove anything that sounds like it is not you. Write 3 versions of a follow-up email: Short (max 40 words), Normal (max 80 words), Firm (max 80 words, still polite).

Facts:
- Sender: Karan
- Receiver: Ms Iyer from a vendor company
- We sent Purchase Order 2291 on 12 October.
- We have not received a delivery date.
- Goal: get a confirmed delivery date by Friday.

Each version needs a subject line. Use simple English. No emojis. Sign off as Karan.
Turn messy meeting notes into an action list

2.02 Automate office work Paste the notes. Get owners, tasks and dates in a table. Make an action table from rough notes After a meeting, notes are usually a mess of half sentences. The real value is the list of who does what by when . AI is very good at pulling this out. Tell the AI what to do when something is missing, for example "if no owner is named, write Unassigned". Otherwise it may guess. A guessed owner is worse than a blank one. Send the table to the group the same day. People forget decisions fast. A clear list stops follow-up calls. Turn these meeting notes into an action table.

Notes:
"Team sync, Monday. Priya will update the leave tracker by Wednesday. We agreed to move the monthly review to the 28th. Someone should book the meeting room for the review. Arjun to share the new template, he said Friday. Budget for training still not decided, discuss next week."

Output format:
1. A table with columns: Task, Owner, Due date.
2. If no owner is named, write Unassigned. If no date is named, write Not set. Do not guess.
3. Then a list called "Decisions" and a list called "Open questions".
Clean data and get Google Sheets formulas

2.03 Automate office work Describe your columns in words. Get the exact formula back. Clean names and turn text amounts into numbers You do not need to remember formulas. You need to describe the problem clearly: which column has what, and what you want in the result. Tell the AI the cell addresses and show 2 sample rows. Then ask for the formula for row 2 so you can fill it down. Always test the formula on the sample rows first. If the result is wrong, paste the wrong result back and say what you expected. I use Google Sheets. Column A has names with extra spaces and wrong capital letters. Column B has amounts typed as text with a rupee sign and commas.

Sample rows:
A2: "  ravi KUMAR "   B2: "₹12,500"
A3: "meena  shah"     B3: "₹8,250"

Give me two formulas for row 2 that I can fill down:
1. In C2: the clean name, like "Ravi Kumar".
2. In D2: the amount as a real number, like 12500.
Show the formula only, then one line explaining how it works.
Write the weekly report from raw numbers

2.04 Automate office work Numbers in. Five clear lines for your manager out. You check the maths. Make a 5-line weekly update A weekly update is the same shape every time: what happened, how it compares to last week, what is the risk, what is next. Give the AI the numbers and this shape. Check the maths. Chatbots can add up numbers wrongly. Do a quick sum on your phone calculator, or ask the chatbot to show its working in one line. Ask for plain words. Managers read on phones too. Short lines win. Write a weekly update for my manager in exactly 5 lines.

Data (support requests closed per day this week): Monday 42, Tuesday 38, Wednesday 51, Thursday 47, Friday 40.
Last week's total: 205.

Lines to write:
1. Total closed this week and the daily average (1 decimal).
2. Change versus last week, in number and percent (1 decimal).
3. The busiest day.
4. One risk: Wednesday was heavy, so staffing may be thin on busy days.
5. Next step: review the staffing plan for peak days.

Show your working for the numbers in one short line at the end. Use plain words.
Summarise a long document without losing the key points

2.05 Automate office work Read 20 pages in 3 minutes, then check the parts that matter. Summarise a leave policy in 4 lines For long files, use a tool that works from your own document . Google's Gemini Notebook (it used to be called NotebookLM) has a free plan. You upload a PDF or paste text, and it answers only from that source. It also shows which part of the source each answer came from. Whatever tool you use, ask for the same four things: the main point , what I must do , deadlines or numbers , and what is unclear . Do not upload confidential files to a free tool unless your company allows it. When in doubt, use a sample or ask your IT team. Summarise the policy below for an employee.

Output exactly:
1. Main point (1 line)
2. What I must do (up to 3 bullets)
3. Dates and numbers (bullets)
4. What is unclear (bullets; write "Nothing" if clear)

Policy text:
"Employees get 18 days of paid leave each year. Leave must be requested at least 3 working days before the start date, except for emergencies. Unused leave, up to 6 days, can be carried over to the next year. Leave for more than 5 days in a row needs the manager's written approval. The leave year runs from 1 April."
Write a post that sounds like you

3.01 Make content Three rough bullets and one writing sample. That is all the AI needs. Turn 3 bullets into a short post AI posts often sound the same: "In today's fast-paced world...". People skip them. The fix is your own voice. Give the AI a sample of how you really write, and your real point. A good post has three parts: a hook (first line that makes people stop), one useful idea , and one small ask (a question or a save). Tell the AI what to avoid. A short "do not use" list works well: no hashtags, no emojis, no buzzwords. Then change a few words so it is truly yours. Write a short social media post (under 90 words) from these bullets.

Bullets:
- I used to spend 40 minutes every Friday on my weekly report.
- Now I paste my numbers into a chatbot and it takes 8 minutes.
- I still check every number myself.

My writing style (copy this tone): "I tried this for a month. It worked, with one catch. Here is what I learned."

Structure: a first line that makes people stop, 2 or 3 short lines of detail, and a closing question.
Do not use: hashtags, emojis, the words "game-changer" or "fast-paced world". Give me 2 versions.
Write a 30-second video script with a strong hook

3.02 Make content Put the useful part in the first 2 seconds. Then keep every line short. Script: 3 Google Sheets shortcuts in 30 seconds Short videos win or lose in the first two seconds. Start with the result or the problem. Do not start with "Hi guys, welcome to my channel." A 30-second script has about 70 to 80 spoken words. Break it into four beats: Hook (0 to 3 seconds), Step 1, 2, 3 (3 to 25 seconds) and Close (25 to 30 seconds). Ask the AI to write what is spoken and what is on screen in two columns. This tells you what to record. Write a 30-second vertical video script for working people in India: "3 Google Sheets shortcuts that save time".

Rules:
- Total spoken words between 65 and 80.
- Beats with time ranges: Hook (0-5s), Tip 1, Tip 2, Tip 3, Close (26-30s).
- The hook must show the result, not greet the viewer. The Tips share the time from 5s to 26s.
- Three real shortcuts for Windows: Ctrl+Shift+V (paste values only), Ctrl+; (insert today's date), Ctrl+Space (select column).
- Table with columns: Time, Spoken line, On screen text.
- Plain Indian English. No hashtags. No emojis.
Turn an idea into a good image prompt

3.03 Make content Say what is in the picture, how it looks and what must not be there. Ask the chatbot to write the image prompt for you Free image tools exist inside several chatbots. A weak image prompt is "nice office photo". A strong one names five things: subject , setting , style , camera or framing and mood or colours . Add an avoid line for things you do not want, for example "no text, no logos". AI images often spell words wrongly. Add real text later in a free editor such as Canva or your phone's photo app. Never make an image of a real person without their permission. Use made-up people or objects for your posts. The quality of free tools and their limits change often, so try two tools and keep the better result. I need a background image for a social media post about saving time at work. Write one detailed image prompt I can paste into an image generator.

Include these 5 parts as one flowing paragraph: subject, setting, style, framing, colours and mood.
Idea: a neat desk with a laptop showing a simple spreadsheet, a cup of tea and a small clock.
Style: clean flat illustration.
Format: square, with empty space at the top for text.
Add an "Avoid:" sentence at the end. Do not include any real person or brand.
Give me only the prompt.

3.04 Make content Write for the ear, not for the eye. Then cut the words into caption lines. Clean a script and split it into caption lines Spoken words are not the same as written words. Short sentences, simple words and a clear pause between ideas. Read your script out loud once. If you run out of breath, split the sentence. You can record your own voice on your phone. That feels more real than a robot voice, and it is free. If you use a text-to-speech tool, check its terms and choose a natural voice. Captions matter because many people watch with the sound off. Keep each caption line to 6 words or fewer , and break at natural pauses. Here is my rough script:
"So basically what I did was I put my weekly numbers into a chatbot and then it made the summary for me which saved me around thirty minutes every single week."

Do two things:
1. Rewrite it as a clean voiceover: short sentences, simple words, natural pauses shown with "...". Keep my meaning and add nothing new.
2. Split the clean version into caption lines. Each line must have 6 words or fewer. Number the lines.
Plan a week of content in 10 minutes

3.05 Make content One topic, five angles, one clear plan you can follow. Make a 5-day plan for freshers starting their first job Posting daily is hard when you start from a blank page every morning. Plan once, post all week. Pick one audience and one theme . Then turn that theme into five angles: a tip, a mistake, a story, a tool and a question. Ask for a table. For each day you need three things: the idea , the format (text, image, short video) and the first line (the hook). Keep it small. Five posts you really make beat thirty you never finish. Write them in one sitting, then schedule them using your phone's free tools. Make a 5-day content plan (Monday to Friday) for people in their first year at an office job in India.

Theme: "Small habits that make you look reliable".
Use these five angles, one per day: a tip, a common mistake, a short story, a free tool, a question for the audience.

Output a table with columns: Day, Angle, Format (text, image or short video), Idea in one line, First line (hook, under 12 words).
No hashtags. No emojis. Do not mention any company.

4.01 Build small tools You do not need to code. You need a clear one-page idea. Write a one-page spec for a small tool Today you can describe a small tool in plain words and an AI will write the code. People call this vibe coding . It works well for small, simple tools: a calculator, a checklist, a form, a Sheets helper. It works only when you are clear about three things: who uses it , what goes in and what comes out . This is a spec. A one-page spec is the most valuable thing you can write. AI-written code can have bugs and security gaps. Start with tools that do not store private data. Test with simple numbers you can check by hand. Help me write a one-page spec for a small web tool called "Bill Splitter".

The tool: friends enter the total bill, the number of people and a tip percent. It shows the amount each person pays.

Write the spec with these headings: Who uses it, Inputs, Output, 3 test cases with exact numbers, What it must NOT do.
Rules: Work out the test case answers carefully. Keep the whole spec under 150 words. The tool must not store or send any data.
Build a working calculator page in one file

4.02 Build small tools One prompt. One HTML file. Open it in your browser. Build a loan EMI calculator A web page can be a single file. You save the text as emi.html and open it on your phone or computer. No server, no account, no cost. Ask the AI for one file with HTML, CSS and JavaScript together. Ask for plain code with no external libraries. This keeps it small and easy to check. Then test. Type the exact numbers whose answer you know. If the result is wrong, tell the AI the numbers you typed, the answer you got and the answer you expected. Write a single-file HTML page: a loan EMI calculator.

Inputs: loan amount in rupees, yearly interest rate in percent, number of months.
Outputs: monthly EMI and total interest, shown in Indian number format (for example 23,072).
Rules:
- One file with HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No libraries, no internet calls.
- Big input boxes and a big button that work well on a phone.
- Use the standard formula: EMI = P x r x (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1), where r is the monthly rate.
- Handle a 0 percent rate without an error.
- Give me only the code.
Automate Google Sheets with a small script

4.03 Build small tools Highlight overdue rows by itself. The AI writes the script. You run it once. Colour overdue tasks pink Google Sheets has a free built-in tool called Apps Script . It runs small programs on your sheet. You do not install anything. Open your sheet and choose Extensions, then Apps Script. Describe your sheet exactly: the column letters, the header names and what each column holds. Then say what should happen. The AI writes the script. A script can change your data. Make a copy of your sheet first. Run the script on the copy. The first run asks you to give permission. Read what it asks, and only allow it for your own sheet. Write a Google Apps Script function named highlightOverdue for my active sheet.

My sheet: row 1 is the header. Column A = Task, B = Owner, C = Due date (a real date), D = Status (values: Open, Done).
Behaviour: for each row from row 2, if the due date is before today and the status is not "Done", set the background of columns A to D to pink. Otherwise clear the background.
Rules: Compare dates without the time part. Do not delete or edit any values. Add a short comment before each step. Give me only the code, and 3 steps to run it.
Make one-tap WhatsApp message links from a Sheet

4.04 Build small tools No paid tool. No API. A formula builds the message and you tap send. Build payment reminder links WhatsApp has a simple link format: https://wa.me/ followed by the phone number with country code, and an optional ?text= message. When you tap the link, WhatsApp opens with the message ready. You press send. A Google Sheets formula can build these links for every row. This is not bulk messaging. You still tap each one, so each message goes to a person who knows you. Do not use it to spam people who did not ask to hear from you. Use only contact details you have a right to use. Keep numbers in a column without spaces or plus signs. Start them with the country code, 91 for India. I use Google Sheets. Row 1 has headers. Columns: A = Phone (10 digits, no spaces), B = Name, C = Amount (number), D = Due date (a real date).

Write one formula for E2 that makes a clickable link labelled "Send on WhatsApp". It must open https://wa.me/91 plus the phone number, with this ready message:
"Hi [Name], your invoice of Rs [Amount] is due on [day month, like 5 Nov]. Please confirm payment. Thanks!"

Use HYPERLINK and ENCODEURL so the spaces and symbols work. Show the formula only, then the link it will build for my row 2 data.
AI agents explained simply: plan one on paper

4.05 Build small tools An agent is a helper that works in steps. Plan the steps before you trust it. Plan a weekly inbox clean-up agent An AI agent is a chatbot that can take several steps toward a goal and use tools, such as search, email or a spreadsheet, along the way. A normal chatbot answers once. An agent keeps going until it thinks the job is done. That power needs limits. Every good agent plan has five parts: Goal , Tools it may use , Steps , Stop rule (when it must stop) and Human check (what you approve before anything is sent or deleted). Start on paper. If you cannot write the steps for a person to follow, an agent will not manage them either. Start with read-only jobs, such as sorting and summarising. Add actions like sending or deleting only after you trust it. Help me design a safe AI agent plan, on paper only, for this job: "Every Monday, go through my unread work emails from last week and give me a short list of what needs a reply."

Write these five headings with short answers: Goal, Tools it may use, Steps (max 5), Stop rule, Human check.
Safety rules to build in: it may only read and summarise. It must never send, delete or move any email. It must not open attachments or links.
Keep it under 120 words.

5.01 Small business Clear lines with price, size and delivery. Customers decide without asking. Turn a rough product list into catalogue lines Customers on WhatsApp ask the same questions again and again. How much? What size? Do you deliver? A good catalogue line answers all three before they ask. Give the AI your rough list: product names, prices in ₹, sizes and your delivery rules. Ask for one short line per product, always in the same order: name , size , price and one plain benefit . Add the delivery note once, at the end. Check every price and size before you post. The AI can change a number or add a claim you cannot keep, such as "best in town" or "100% organic". Delete anything that is not true. Do not put your UPI ID or bank details in the prompt. Add them yourself when you send the catalogue. Role: You write clear WhatsApp catalogue text for small Indian shops.
Task: Turn my rough list into catalogue lines.
Context: I run Meera's Home Bakery in Pune. My rough list:
- chocolate cake 500g 450, 1kg 850
- whole wheat banana bread 400g loaf 220
- nankhatai box of 12, 180
- eggless option on all cakes, 50 extra
Delivery: free within 3 km, Rs 40 beyond that, order one day before.
Format: One line per product: name, size, price in Rs, one short plain benefit. Then one delivery line. Then one line that asks customers to reply with their order. Simple English. No emojis. No claims like "best" or "healthiest". Under 100 words.
Reply to customers fast and politely

5.02 Small business Write a small set of ready replies once. Use them every day. Make four reply templates for your shop Most customer messages are of a few types: price questions, "where is my order", complaints and refund requests. Write a ready reply for each type once. Keep them in a notes app so you can copy them fast. Ask the AI for templates with blanks like [name] and [date]. You fill the blanks each time. That keeps every reply personal and correct. A good reply to a problem has three parts: say sorry or thanks , say what you will do and say when . Do not promise what you cannot do, such as a refund that your rules do not allow. Put your shop rules in the prompt: delivery time, return days and how you pay refunds. Then the AI writes replies that match them. Role: You write polite WhatsApp replies for a small Indian shop.
Task: Write 4 reply templates: 1) price question, 2) order is late, 3) complaint about wrong size, 4) refund request.
Context: Shop: Rani Boutique, Jaipur. We stitch and sell women's kurtas. Our rules: free size alteration within 7 days of purchase. Exchange within 7 days if unused. Refund only if we cannot fix or exchange the item. Refunds go back by UPI within 3 working days.
Format: Each template under 50 words. Use blanks like [name], [item], [price], [date]. Warm, simple English. No emojis. Do not promise anything outside our rules.

5.03 Small business Let the AI write the picture prompt and the offer text. You put the words on the picture. Make a Diwali offer poster for a sweet shop A festival poster has two parts: the picture and the words . Make them separately. Image tools often spell words wrongly, so ask for a picture with no text at all. Ask the chatbot for both in one go: an image prompt that leaves empty space for text, and the short poster text. Paste the image prompt into a free image tool. Free image tools exist inside several chatbots. Then open a free editor such as Canva free. Add the picture and type the poster text on top yourself. Keep it short: the offer, the dates, the shop name and how to order. People look at a poster for only a few seconds. Use only your own shop name and logo. Do not copy another brand's design. Do not use photos of real people without their permission. Role: You help small Indian shops make festival posters.
Task: Give me two things.
1) An image prompt for a free image tool. Square picture for a Diwali sweets offer: a brass plate of mixed Indian sweets, small diyas, marigold flowers, warm golden light. Leave the top third empty for text. Avoid: any text, letters, numbers, logos or people.
2) Poster text that I will add myself in Canva. Shop: Gupta Mithai, Indore. Offer: 10% off all sweet boxes, 1 Nov to 10 Nov. Orders on WhatsApp: [your number].
Format: Poster text in 4 short lines, max 6 words each. Simple English.
Turn rough notes into a quote

5.04 Small business Type the job in your own words. Get a clean table with a total. Then check every number. Make a quote for an AC repair job Many quotes start as rough notes on paper or in a chat: "2 AC service, 1 gas refill, 1 stand". The AI can turn these notes into a neat table with item , quantity , rate and amount , plus a total. AI can make maths mistakes. Check every row yourself: quantity times rate must equal the amount. Then add the amounts and match the total. The calculator on your phone is enough. This is a quote or a simple bill draft. It is not a GST tax invoice . A tax invoice needs some fields by law. If you need one, add those fields yourself, or ask your accountant. Do not paste a customer's phone number, address or your bank details into the chatbot. Use placeholders and fill them in later. Role: You help a small repair shop write clear quotes.
Task: Turn my rough notes into a quote table.
Context: Shop: Kumar Cool Services, Coimbatore. Customer: [customer name]. Notes:
- AC general service, 2 units, 600 each
- gas refill, 1 unit, 2500
- outdoor unit stand, 1, 1200
- labour for stand fitting, 400
Format: Title "Quotation". Then a table with columns: No., Item, Qty, Rate (Rs), Amount (Rs). Then a Total row. Then 2 short lines: valid for 7 days, and payment by UPI or cash after the work. Do not add tax. Do not add any item I did not list.

5.05 Small business Paste your reviews. See what customers keep saying. Fix one thing this week. Find the themes in a salon's reviews and reply to a bad one One review is one opinion. Ten reviews show a pattern. If four people mention long waiting, that is the first thing to fix. Copy 10 to 20 recent reviews from Google or from WhatsApp messages into the chatbot. Remove customer names and phone numbers first. Ask for themes : what people like, what they complain about and which reviews mention each one. Check the result yourself. The AI can miscount or put a review in the wrong group. Read the reviews in each group and see if they really say the same thing. Reply to a bad review in calm words. Thank them, say sorry for the exact problem, say what you will change and invite them back. Change the reply so it says only what you will really do. Do not argue, and do not offer a discount for removing the review. Role: You help a small salon owner understand customer reviews.
Task: 1) Group these reviews into themes, with review numbers. 2) Give the top 2 things to fix. 3) Write a reply to review 4.
Reviews:
1. Good haircut, but I waited 40 minutes.
2. Very clean salon, friendly staff.
3. Great facial. Fair price.
4. Booked for 5 pm, served at 6 pm. Nobody told me. Not coming back.
5. Polite staff. Long wait on Sundays.
6. Nice threading, quick service.
7. AC not working, very hot inside.
8. Clean place, good hair colour.
9. Long wait even with a booking.
10. Friendly staff, fair price.
Format: Reply under 60 words, polite, no excuses. Simple English.
Plan a 40-minute lesson in five parts

6.01 Teachers and students Give the class, the topic and the time. Get a lesson plan you can teach tomorrow. Plan a Class 8 Science lesson on photosynthesis A good lesson plan answers five questions. What will students learn? How do I start? What will they do? How do I check they understood? What do they do at home? Call these the objective , warm-up , activity , check and homework . AI can draft all five in a minute. It does not know your class. So tell it the class, the topic, the time, the class size and what you have in the room. A plan for 45 students with only a blackboard looks very different from a plan for a lab. Ask for minutes next to each part. Then the plan fits your period, and you can see at once if one part is too long. You are still the teacher. Read the plan, change what does not suit your students, and check every fact against your textbook. Role: You are an experienced school Science teacher in India.
Task: Plan one 40-minute lesson on photosynthesis for Class 8.
Context: 40 students. I have a blackboard, chalk and some leaves from the school garden. No projector. Students know that plants need water and sunlight, but not why.
Format: Use exactly these parts, each with minutes:
1. Objective (1 sentence)
2. Warm-up
3. Activity (pairs or groups)
4. Check (3 quick questions with answers)
5. Homework (one short task)

What never to paste, how to spot a fake voice or video, and how to check an answer before you trust it. Never paste these A chatbot is not a locked diary. What you type can be stored, and on many free plans it can be used to improve the tool. Treat every chat like a message to a stranger. OTPs, PINs and passwords Aadhaar, PAN, passport or bank account numbers Card numbers, CVV or UPI PIN Other people's phone numbers, addresses or health details Your company's private files, client lists or prices, unless your company allows it Need help with a real document? Replace names and numbers with placeholders first, like [customer name] or [amount]. The answer is just as useful. Check before you trust AI can sound sure and still be wrong. It can invent a fact, a number, a law or a link. Use this routine for anything that matters: Ask it: "Which parts of your answer are you not sure about?" Check every number, date, name and law in a source you trust: an official website, your own records or an expert. Open every link it gives. If the page does not exist or does not say the same thing, do not use it. For health, money and legal questions, use AI to prepare your questions, then ask a doctor, a bank or a lawyer. Fake voices, fake videos AI can copy a voice from a short clip and make a video of a real face. Scammers use this to sound like a relative, a boss or an officer who needs money fast. Urgency is the warning sign. "Send money now", "do not tell anyone" or "your account will be blocked" means stop. Call back on a number you already have. Not the number that called you. Agree a family code word that only you know. Ask for it on any strange call. No real officer asks for money on a video call. Police and courts do not "arrest" people on WhatsApp. If something goes wrong If you lost money to a fraud in India, call the cyber crime helpline 1930 at once, or report it at cybercrime.gov.in . Then call your bank. Fast reports give the best chance to stop the money. Use AI at work, the right way Follow your company's AI rules. If there are none, ask your manager before you paste work files. You are responsible for what you send, even if AI wrote the first draft. Say when AI helped, if your school or workplace asks you to.
